title: The previous winner
style: cinematic horror film still, buzzing fluorescent-lit storage unit corridors and a cramped city apartment at night, an eerily detailed handmade dollhouse, dust in the air, sickly green and warm tungsten tones, dramatic moody lighting, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 4. Everyone who ever bought Lot 47 sold it within a week. Then they ran. 📦

Original fiction. Part 5 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: the faceless figure in the dollhouse moved each night, and whatever it did, something did in Gina's real apartment.
scenes.image: faceless carved wooden figure standing at the foot of a tiny dollhouse bed

scenes.narration: Gina drives back to the auction yard. The auctioneer sees her coming and closes his eyes.
scenes.image: tired auctioneer in a windbreaker closing his eyes at the door of a small storage facility office

scenes.narration: He keeps records. Lot 47 has sold eleven times in nine years. Always under fifty dollars. Always to someone new.
scenes.image: cluttered auction office with stacked old ledgers and a desk lamp, an old man leaning over the desk

scenes.narration: Every buyer put it back up for auction within a week. Every single one. And then they moved away. Some left their furniture behind.
scenes.image: empty apartment with furniture abandoned under dust sheets, a door left open, afternoon light

scenes.narration: She calls one. A man named Curtis, three states away. He answers on the first ring. Is it still a model of your place? Then you've got time.
scenes.image: woman on a phone in her car in a storage yard at dusk, worried face lit by the dashboard

scenes.narration: Time for what? It's not a model of your home, he says. It's a model of where it lives. Every day it gets a little more right.
scenes.image: nervous middle-aged man in a motel room far away holding a phone to his ear, curtains drawn

scenes.narration: How'd you get rid of it? Same as everyone. You sell it. It only stays with the owner.
scenes.image: close-up of the woman gripping her phone, knuckles pale, rain beginning on the windshield

scenes.narration: One more thing, he says. If the little man is ever at the window, looking out, it's already picked the next buyer. Don't let them in.
scenes.image: dollhouse front window seen up close at night, dark glass, tiny curtains

scenes.narration: When Gina gets home, the figure is standing at the tiny front window. Pressed to the glass. Facing the street.
scenes.image: faceless carved figure pressed against a tiny dollhouse window, looking out, lamp light behind it
apartment front door at night seen from a dark hallway, a thin line of light beneath it and a shadow of feet
